column1: # Every place in test code that asks which Iceberg line the build is (IcebergLine.current(),
# IcebergV3.supported(), the openhouse.iceberg.line property), with how many times the same line
# occurs in the file and why. A test that expects one thing on the reference line (LinkedIn
# Iceberg 1.5.2) and another on the default line (Iceberg 1.12) accepts a difference of the
# default line; such a branch is listed here as "difference from main", with its cause, so that
# every one is reviewed in one place. What scripts/ci/check-iceberg-line-branches.py enforces: a
# branch the list does not name fails, so does an entry whose branch is gone, an entry whose
# count is not the number of times the line occurs, and an entry without a known kind or a reason.
# It does not check that a branch still differs between the lines: a "difference from main" whose
# two answers became equal, and an assumption that skips a test, are found only by reading.
#   difference from main     the default line answers differently from LinkedIn main here
#   declared difference      the branch selects entries of a declared-difference list
#   one line has the feature the test is of something only one line has (format v3 metadata, the
#                            Iceberg 1.12 endpoint list); not a difference from main
#   Iceberg client version   Iceberg's own REST client differs by version on a route LinkedIn
#                            main does not have; not a difference from main
#   detection                tests the line detection itself
# file<TAB>the line, trimmed<TAB>occurrences in the file<TAB>kind<TAB>reason

The Spark 3.5 OpenHouse catalog declares the column-defaults capability on the reference line only, so on the default line a create that requires it is refused (422 CLIENT_CAPABILITY_MISSING) unless a declaring catalog stands in; on LinkedIn main the catalog always declared it.

CREATE TABLE with format-version 3 on a cluster with the switch off: Iceberg 1.12's client builds the metadata and the service stores the table at version 2 (the service answers as LinkedIn main does); LinkedIn's 1.5.2 client refuses before any request, as on main.

The column-defaults capability over the Iceberg REST routes: the engine catalog declares it on the reference line only (as in CatalogPluginContractTest).
Iceberg REST routes: RESTCatalog 1.5.2 rebuilds the loaded metadata and stamps last-updated-ms (first use), and checks table existence by loading the table (second use); 1.12 does neither.
View existence over the Iceberg REST routes: 1.12 asks the exists route, 1.5.2 loads the view.
View rename over the Iceberg REST routes: 1.5.2 sends it and raises the 406 as RESTException; 1.12 reads the endpoint list and refuses before sending.

A row delta that only adds delete files (a merge-on-read DELETE) is named by Iceberg's BaseRowDelta: "overwrite" on 1.5.2 as on LinkedIn main, "delete" on 1.12. The operation is the client's, so it is the same through the OpenHouse catalog: snapshots.operation of a merge-on-read DELETE reads "delete" on the default line. The recorded write statements have no merge-on-read DELETE.
